correctness.rationale: For each active count pair, edge counts are C(x,2)y and xC(y,2), giving p=(x-1)/(s-2), E[d_next]=((s-3)/(s-2))d. The exact gamma product p_k makes d_k/p_k a stopped martingale; its quadratic variation normalized by 2n tends to one by a gamma-ratio Riemann sum, while the drift-square correction has expected total O(\(n^{1/2}\)) and normalized increments are o(1). Doob bounds exclude absorption above \(n^{1/2}\), and below n^(1/8) the surviving event would force the Gaussian-normalized martingale to vanish, an asymptotically null event. The martingale varies by o_P(sqrt(n)) in that boundary layer, and at jamming R=s=|d|. Thus R/(2n)^(1/4) converges to |N(0,1)|^(3/2). Full edge counts and gamma products were checked on actual embedded proof code; 622 exact-rational/computational checks passed. Finite checks are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The residual unoccupied count is the natural terminal observable for three-site adsorption. The balanced two-class capacity constraint produces a genuinely nonstandard \(n^{1/4}\) terminal scale and explicit power-of-folded-normal law, unlike fixed-size complete-substrate residuals or the earlier cross-composition full-cover Gaussian profile. The result gives a physically interpretable mean-field jamming universality mechanism from an exact martingale and identifies a new limiting law, not a parameter increment or routine table.
